name: Macromolecular X-ray diffraction data collection at 100 K on a loop-mounted, liquid-nitrogen flash-cooled protein crystal in an Oxford Cryostream
plain_name: Collect X-ray diffraction from a protein crystal kept at 100 K
description: A cryoprotected protein crystal mounted in a nylon loop is flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen and kept at 100 K in an open-flow nitrogen gas stream on the goniometer while diffraction images are recorded; cooling below the glass transition of water (about 136-155 K) limits radiation damage.
keywords: Collect X-ray diffraction from a protein crystal kept at 100 K

sources.citation: Kumar A, Karthikeyan S (2018). Crystal structure of the MSMEG_4306 gene product from Mycobacterium smegmatis. Acta Crystallographica Section F. doi:10.1107/s2053230x18002236
Pflugrath JW (2015). Practical macromolecular cryocrystallography. Acta Crystallographica Section F. doi:10.1107/s2053230x15008304

reported_equipment: Rigaku MicroMax-007 HF rotating-anode X-ray generator

requirements.rationale: Diffraction data are collected with the crystal at 100 K.
The crystal must be held below the lower bound of the water glass-transition range (about 136 K).
Crystals are flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen before data collection.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
